transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (Redwood), Michael Chen (Northstar Head of ML), Priya Patel (SRE), Aaron Wallace (Product), Jin Li (SecOps)

Summary: quick scoping call for a 4-week POC focusing on workload characterization and traffic modeling for Northstar Lending's document ingestion and loan decisioning assistant. Goals: define success criteria (latency/quality/cost), exchange sample traffic, run baseline benchmarks, align timeline for Dedicated vs Private deployment options.

Topics: workload sizing, QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, batching and caching, quantization tradeoffs, security/compliance needs, POC timeline and deliverables.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sam Carter: Hey everyone thanks for joining, hi Michael, Priya, Aaron, Jin. We got Lina and Ravi from infra, we'll focus on the workload modeling piece today.
[00:18] Michael Chen: Hey Sam, thanks. We basically want to understand whether Redwood can run our loan chat assistant at peak times and what the unit costs would be. We currently run an internal LLM for triage but latency's been all over the place.
[00:30] Lina Gomez: Cool, quick agenda - gather production QPS/concurrency, sample token distributions, define SLOs (p95 latency, tail), success criteria, then agree POC steps. Sound good?
[00:42] Priya Patel: Yep. Also SecOps will need to validate encryption/KMS and audit log retention. Jin will jump in on that.
[00:50] Jin Li: yeah. we need SSO, SAML, RBAC, and a runbook for data residency. Prefer private deployment or VPC peered endpoints.
[01:05] Sam Carter: Understood. Michael, can you give us current traffic numbers and the expected peaks?
[01:14] Michael Chen: Sure, average QPS for the assistant is about 1.5 right now. Peak during end-of-month runs at ~28 QPS for about 45 minutes. We expect growth to 50 QPS in six months as we roll out to internal ops and partners. Concurrency per instance is around 20 active chats and we usually see bursts up to 120 concurrent sessions across our fleet.
[01:37] Lina Gomez: ok so spikes matter. Can you describe input token sizes and output lengths?
[01:44] Aaron Wallace: Typical input prompt is 120-240 tokens (user message + recent context). Output is usually 40-120 tokens for short answers, but for decisioning flows we sometimes stream 300-600 tokens. About 12% of requests are long form.
[02:02] Ravi Shah: got it. For modeling we'll use distribution buckets: short (<64), medium (64-256), long (>256). Sounds like 70/18/12 split roughly.
[02:15] Michael Chen: That matches our logs. Also we have reranking jobs for batch scoring overnight that hit very high token counts but low QPS - maybe outside this POC scope?
[02:26] Priya Patel: we'd like to include one reranking scenario as an anchor for throughput tests.
[02:30] Lina Gomez: fine, include a scheduled batch test for throughput/quantization evals.

[00:03:00] Sam Carter: Let's talk success criteria. From Redwood's side we've seen customers pick p95 latency < 300ms for short prompts on Dedicated, and p95 < 600ms on hosted for mixed loads. What are your targets?
[03:20] Michael Chen: Target p95 under 350ms for short prompts, under 700ms for mixed. For cost we'd like to see cost per 1k short requests below $X (we'll share budget), and quality parity with our current model - F1/regression metrics TBD. If those hold we move to a 3-month trial.
[03:42] Sam Carter: Ok so we'll aim to show baseline with Hosted first then run a Dedicated pilot if it improves latency/cost. For private, we'll validate network and KMS.
[03:55] Aaron Wallace: timeline?
[03:58] Lina Gomez: Proposed POC: week 0 (this week) - onboarding and data exchange; week 1 - baseline hosted benchmarks (latency and token costs) using customer-provided 48h sample; week 2 - tuning (batching, caching, quant profiles), run Dedicated pilot if needed; week 3 - run extended load and regression evals; week 4 - final report + handoff. So ~4 weeks end-to-end.
[04:28] Michael Chen: That works. What instrumentation will you need?
[04:32] Ravi Shah: We'll need a sample of traffic (48h), schema for requests/responses, list of heavy-offenders (long prompts), and a few evaluation prompts. We'll also ask for ground-truth labels for quality tests.
[04:45] Priya Patel: For security we'll need an initial security questionnaire. We'll review SOC2 and encryption details.
[04:51] Jin Li: Also network topology - we prefer a VPC peered deployment for the POC; is that supported?
[04:58] Lina Gomez: Yes, VPC peering for Redwood Private is supported. For hosted we can set up private endpoints and mTLS. Note - some product names in our docs show Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Dedi... the right one is Redwood Dedicated, sorry if transcriber mangled it.
[05:16] Michael Chen: Any recommended model family? We use a mix of open models currently but need a model that supports tool-calling and structured output.
[05:24] Lina Gomez: We'll recommend a 7B+ quantized variant for short/medium latency sensitive flows and a 13B variant for higher-quality decisioning. We'll run A/B between quant levels to show cost/quality tradeoffs.
[05:36] Sam Carter: Quick note on caching - prefix/KV caching can reduce token compute for repeated context. Given your high session concurrency, caching and batching should give a sizable cost win. We'll instrument cache hit rates in the POC.
[05:49] Aaron Wallace: Great. What about burst handling?
[05:52] Ravi Shah: Smart routing: we can route to a cheaper compatible model when Dedicated is saturated, or to another region. For the POC we'll simulate bursts matching your 28-50 QPS peaks and longer tails up to 120 concurrent sessions.
[06:07] Michael Chen: Benchmarks — what will you measure exactly?
[06:10] Lina Gomez: We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1k requests, cache hit rate, and quality metrics (BLEU/F1 or task-specific metrics). We'll provide the benchmark harness and results spreadsheet.
[06:25] Priya Patel: We need audit logs and TTL for logs - retention for 1 year in our compliance.
[06:31] Jin Li: Also KMS integration - we require customer-managed keys for the private deployment.
[06:35] Sam Carter: That's fine. We'll surface our KMS/HSM options and how keys are rotated, and provide SOC2/ISO artifacts.

[06:45] Aaron Wallace: Ok, pricing ballpark?
[06:48] Sam Carter: We'll send POC pricing + assumptions. Pilot pricing usually covers reserved Dedicated during the run and a small ingestion fee for hosted tests. Exact numbers in SOW.

[07:00] Michael Chen: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:03] Lina Gomez: None immediate. We'll need the traffic sample and credentials to a staging environment. If you want Private on-prem, that adds 2-3 extra days for infra provisioning but still doable inside the 4 week window if the customer provides network access quickly.

[07:20] Sam Carter: Recap / next steps: 1) Michael to send 48h sample traffic + eval prompts by 7/21; 2) Sam to share SOW/pricing by 7/22; 3) Lina will run baseline hosted benchmarks by 7/24 and share spreadsheet; 4) Jin to send compliance checklist and network doc by 7/23; 5) schedule private deployment deep-dive week of 7/27.
[07:48] Michael Chen: sounds good. We'll also include a reranking batch sample for throughput.
[07:53] Sam Carter: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the SOW.
[08:00] (call ends)
